Shall we, the storm-tossed sailors, weep

For those who may not sail again;

Or wisely envy them, and keep

Our pity for the living men?

Beyond the weary waste of sea,

Beyond the wider waste of death,

I strain my gaze and cry to thee

Whose still heart never answereth.

O brother, is thy coral bed

So sweet thou wilt not hear my speech?

This hand, methinks, if I were dead,

To thy dear hand would strive to reach.

I would not, if God gave us choice

For each to bear the other’s part,

That mine should be the silent voice,

And thine the silent, aching heart.

Ah, well for any voyage done,

Whate’er its end, or port, or reef;

Better the voyage ne’er begun,

For all ships sail the sea of Grief.

My fucking God. What an entitled piece of complete shit. There really should be an animal offenders list that bars people with a track record of poor pet care from having animals in the future. Back in Illinois my family rescued our dauchsunds. Marshall when I was 13 (we recently had to let him go, but he was 16.5 and had a great life) and Charlie when I was 17.

In March 2014 I moved to my now fiancés hometown in rural Alaska. He had a ragdoll named Gus that he got because his mom runs the towns animal rescue. Gus had many issues, he wasn't well cared for. This family had a queen named Husky and they wouldn't fix her. She had at least 6 litters that we know of and she's 10. The family went out of town after she gave birth, but left no food or litter boxes. So Gus would eat non food things, and would use fabric as a litter box. Their door blew off during a blizzard and the kittens walked across the road to my fiancés sisters place, as she'd fed them before. She took them all in and brought them to her moms house where they cleaned them up and eventually found homes for them all. Gus was scared and my fiancé had just walked downstairs in his pajamas, and Gus climbed up his pantleg and into his arms. He chose my fiancé as his human.

Gus is lucky he was adopted by my fiancé because I doubt anyone else would be willing to put up with some of his behaviors like eating plastic and rarely using his litter box. But he was such a sweet boy, he'd sleep in Kyle's arms every night all night. He'd sing when kyle got home and meow until he got his hug. Unfortunaly last year he ate some plastic and wasn't able to pass it. We're in a rural town and have no vet. I tried to manually disimpact him as I'd watched the vet do it the year before when he had another plastic obstruction, but it wasn't successful. He passed away last Halloween at 8 years old. I miss Gusum very much.

I really wanted a ragdoll of my very own and had looked into getting one from a breeder but I wanted to adopt one versas buy one if I could. Then a cat came up on the town trading post site that I fell in love with. I emailed them but they said a woman had already gotten him. Turns out the woman who picked him up was Kyle's mom, who runs the rescue. She wanted him to be a shop kitty, but after seeing he was declawed in the front decided she couldn't (she wants shop cats to be able to defend themselves if necessary) She told me the cat was timid and shy but I could go up to the shop (it's a combination pet supply shop, boarding and rescue) to meet the kitty. I opened up the cage and let him sniff me a bit, pet his head. He started purring like crazy and rolled over so I could rub his belly. She came down and was awestruck that this kitty was suddenly so sociable and sweet. That day I took him home. His name originally was Sassy as the first owners thought he was female at birth, which seemed common with Huskys litters as at least 3 were presumed female when they were in fact male. I named this sweet kitty Cheddar. He was 4 years old and super sweet. That was last September.

Now he's my baby and my best friend. He's actually one of Gus' siblings/half siblings. Gus was gen.1 and Cheddar is gen 6. Kyles sister has Mylo, who's gen 4. Pretty much every ragdoll in town descends from Husky.

Cheddar is the sweetest kitty I've met. He sleeps in my arms each night and cuddles with me all day. He knows how to roll over and loves belly rubs and snuggles. He's white with gray splotches, has bright blue eyes and a cute pink nose. I love him so much. I hope to have many great years with him. After Gus passed Kyle was devastated of course, and his mom had recently received a kitten who's mother had been hit by a car. The kitten was feral born and about 5 weeks old. He was probably going to be a shop cat. Kyle liked playing with him and I suggested that we foster him to socialize him for adoption. Of course we became foster failures. Kyle says 'we didn't fail at fostering him, we found him a great home, it just happened to be ours!' 😄 We named the little tabby kitten Calcifer. He just turned 1 recently. He's sweet and silly and just a funny cat to be around. Always makes you smile even if getting into mischief. When the vet was in town we got him fixed, and Cheddar already was.

Basically, I've never purchased a pet. I've only paid adoption fees to rescues. In the case of Cheddar and Calcifer, they cost us nothing as the goal is to find them a home. My soon to be mother in law also doesn't charge us for food or litter so our kitties are literally no expense to us aside from their yearly checkup when the vet comes to town for a week.

Also, sphinxes can have fuzz, and they will groom themselves. Dander doesn't come from the fur, it comes from the dried saliva of the cat, so she'd likely get a kitten, figure out it's not hypoallergenic and dump a poor kitten somewhere.

The family went out of town after she gave birth, but left no food or litter boxes. So Gus would eat non food things, and would use fabric as a litter box. Their door blew off during a blizzard and the kittens walked across the road to my fiancés sisters place, as she'd fed them before. She took them all in and brought them to her moms house where they cleaned them up and eventually found homes for them all. Gus was scared and my fiancé had just walked downstairs in his pajamas, and Gus climbed up his pantleg and into his arms. He chose my fiancé as his human.

Gus is lucky he was adopted by my fiancé because I doubt anyone else would be willing to put up with some of his behaviors like eating plastic and rarely using his litter box. But he was such a sweet boy, he'd sleep in Kyle's arms every night all night. He'd sing when kyle got home and meow until he got his hug. Unfortunaly last year he ate some plastic and wasn't able to pass it. We're in a rural town and have no vet. I tried to manually disimpact him as I'd watched the vet do it the year before when he had another plastic obstruction, but it wasn't successful. He passed away last Halloween at 8 years old. I miss Gusum very much.

I really wanted a ragdoll of my very own and had looked into getting one from a breeder but I wanted to adopt one versas buy one if I could. Then a cat came up on the town trading post site that I fell in love with. I emailed them but they said a woman had already gotten him. Turns out the woman who picked him up was Kyle's mom, who runs the rescue. She wanted him to be a shop kitty, but after seeing he was declawed in the front decided she couldn't (she wants shop cats to be able to defend themselves if necessary) She told me the cat was timid and shy but I could go up to the shop (it's a combination pet supply shop, boarding and rescue) to meet the kitty. I opened up the cage and let him sniff me a bit, pet his head. He started purring like crazy and rolled over so I could rub his belly. She came down and was awestruck that this kitty was suddenly so sociable and sweet. That day I took him home. His name originally was Sassy as the first owners thought he was female at birth, which seemed common with Huskys litters as at least 3 were presumed female when they were in fact male. I named this sweet kitty Cheddar. He was 4 years old and super sweet. That was last September.

Now he's my baby and my best friend. He's actually one of Gus' siblings/half siblings. Gus was gen.1 and Cheddar is gen 6. Kyles sister has Mylo, who's gen 4. Pretty much every ragdoll in town descends from Husky.

Cheddar is the sweetest kitty I've met. He sleeps in my arms each night and cuddles with me all day. He knows how to roll over and loves belly rubs and snuggles. He's white with gray splotches, has bright blue eyes and a cute pink nose. I love him so much. I hope to have many great years with him. After Gus passed Kyle was devastated of course, and his mom had recently received a kitten who's mother had been hit by a car. The kitten was feral born and about 5 weeks old. He was probably going to be a shop cat. Kyle liked playing with him and I suggested that we foster him to socialize him for adoption. Of course we became foster failures. Kyle says 'we didn't fail at fostering him, we found him a great home, it just happened to be ours!' 😄 We named the little tabby kitten Calcifer. He just turned 1 recently. He's sweet and silly and just a funny cat to be around. Always makes you smile even if getting into mischief. When the vet was in town we got him fixed, and Cheddar already was.

Basically, I've never purchased a pet. I've only paid adoption fees to rescues. In the case of Cheddar and Calcifer, they cost us nothing as the goal is to find them a home. My soon to be mother in law also doesn't charge us for food or litter so our kitties are literally no expense to us aside from their yearly checkup when the vet comes to town for a week.

Also, sphinxes can have fuzz, and they will groom themselves. Dander doesn't come from the fur, it comes from the dried saliva of the cat, so she'd likely get a kitten, figure out it's not hypoallergenic and dump a poor kitten somewhere.

I let it sit in the cupboard for a week, then left it in the fridge for another week, fearing the smell and displeasure in eating it. Boy was I wrong. It didn't smell too bad at all, and the taste was excellent. Some cheap, plain-tasting fish I otherwise wouldn't have liked too much [mackerel] took on the flavor of the brine most excellently, plus that nice fermented taste common to all fermented foods. The texture was almost exactly like smoked salmon, which I love.

I used my typical ghetto airseal technique for those without a bubbler: a can with holes poked in it and two hand towels rubber-banded over that. Maybe not a perfect seal, but it's worked well for me every time, including this one. Absolutely no gastrointestinal discomfort at all, and I'm pretty sure I don't get worms. Would recommend for making cheap protein taste good, or for grossing out your squeamish germaphobe friends.

I've been learning a lot about that lately and I find it interesting. But I think u could attribute any bad thing you want to cultural Marxism and I think it's hard to actually be able to trace things back to it. Idk tho. That's just my 2 cents. And I'm not disagreeing with you just adding some food for thought.

I think it's worthwhile for people to learn about standard marxism first to help avoid over labeling. Not many people know about it being more than an economic system. It's also a rhetorical system, an analytical system (a pretty crappy one), and many other things. Really in a way it was all things.

Basically Marx's idea wasn't that Marxism was not guaranteed to succeed (but did believe it was guarenteed to attempt it based on some completely absurd logic) but that the more lofty a goal mankind achieve the more inherently better and that there couldn't be a loftier goal, and I agree, than the idea of replacing every previous institution with the thoughts of one man over his lifetime. The goal, or experiment, was to replace everything from family to academic process to economy and government with one singular institution.

Here's who overarching his ideas were, or he intended them to be. He believed that the logic of the rich and the poor was different and that logic itself was subjective. He didn't really believe that but he believed that logic itself is an institution and as an institution it needed to take a back seat to communism. Therefore the rigidity of logic must die and so the belief that the logic of the rich is different than the poor and is subjective is automatically correct, because if it advances communism it is true.

People need to become more familiar with this absurd logic because this shift in though shifts at a much more foundational level than just the economy. Marxism isn't about economy. It's about using the acceptance of absurdity to win political arguments.
